2607.26935.title: What Does It Take to Detect an AI Agent? Minimal Feature Sets for Behavioral Detection under Browser Automation
2607.26935.paper_summary: Bot detectors deployed at scale treat traffic as binary: human or bot. This assumption breaks when AI agents browse the web through browser automation, a traffic class that is neither and that binary classifiers structurally cannot represent. We present a three-class detection framework distinguishing humans, bots, and AI agents, and show that the binary-vs-agent confusion is architectural: a binary human-vs-bot detector misroutes agent sessions because its label space lacks an agent class. On our controlled benchmark, an MLP binary classifier misclassifies 39.1% of real AI agents as human and a SAINT binary transformer misclassifies 34.5%; adding an explicit agent class yields per-class agent F1 = 1.000 in all 30 runs (3 model families $\times$ 10 seeds). To measure evasion resistance, we construct a five-level evasion ladder spanning passive observation, GAN-generated trajectories, and replay of real human cursor data ($n = 2299$ evasion sessions). Across 10 seeds and 3 model families we observe zero agent misses in 22990 per-seed predictions. The discriminative signal is a browser-automation artifact, not evidence of agent reasoning: Playwright does not emit the raw pointer-move and wheel-delta streams a physical input device produces, and this absence signature survives trajectory manipulation. Exhaustive search over all feature subsets of size 1-5 (9401 GBMs) shows that two behavioral features (mouse_event_rate, teleport_click_ratio) give 100% observed agent recall at every evasion level with agent precision 0.994; five features lift macro-F1 to 0.991. The signal is redundantly encoded: removing teleport_click_ratio leaves agent detection at 100%. The single-feature regime is degenerate, flagging every agent only by collapsing the classifier to always predict "agent". Two features robustly isolate agents; five separate all three traffic classes at macro-F1 $\geq 0.99$.
2607.26935.paper_summary_zh: 機器人檢測器在大規模部署時將流量視為二元：人類或機器人。當 AI 代理通過瀏覽器自動化瀏覽網頁時，這一假設會崩潰，這是一種既不是人類也不是機器人的流量類別，而二元分類器在結構上無法表示。 我們提出了一個三類檢測框架，區分人類、機器人和 AI 代理，並顯示二元與代理的混淆是架構性的：一個二元人類與機器人檢測器因為其標籤空間缺乏代理類別而錯誤路由代理會話。在我們的控制基準上，一個 MLP 二元分類器將 39.1% 的真實 AI 代理錯誤分類為人類，而一個 SAINT 二元Transformer將 34.5% 錯誤分類；添加一個明確的代理類別在所有 30 次運行中產生每類代理 F1 = 1.000（3 個模型系列 $\times$ 10 個種子）。為了測量逃避抵抗力，我們構建了一個五級逃避梯度，涵蓋被動觀察、GAN 生成的軌跡以及真實人類光標數據的重播（$n = 2299$ 逃避會話）。在 10 個種子和 3 個模型系列中，我們觀察到在每個種子預測的 22990 次預測中沒有代理漏檢。區分信號是一種瀏覽器自動化的工件，而不是代理推理的證據：Playwright 不會發出物理輸入設備產生的原始指針移動和滾輪增量流，這一缺失特徵在軌跡操縱中仍然存在。對所有大小為 1-5 的特徵子集進行的徹底搜索（9401 GBMs）顯示，兩個行為特徵（mouse_event_rate, teleport_click_ratio）在每個逃避級別上提供 100% 的觀察代理召回，代理精度為 0.994；五個特徵將宏觀 F1 提升至 0.991。該信號是冗餘編碼的：移除 teleport_click_ratio 使代理檢測保持在 100%。單特徵模式是退化的，僅通過將分類器壓縮為始終預測“代理”來標記每個代理。兩個特徵穩健地隔離代理；五個特徵將所有三個流量類別分開，宏觀 F1 $\geq 0.99$。
